source_title: Microsoft Corporation - Form 10-K (Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2018)
publisher_issuer: Microsoft Corporation (filed with U.S. SEC, EDGAR CIK 0000789019, accession 0001564590-18-019062)
company_context: Microsoft under CEO Satya Nadella (CEO since February 2014) executed a multi-year strategic pivot from a packaged-license, on-premise software model toward a cloud-first, subscription/consumption model anchored by Azure and Office 365. Fiscal 2018 was a year in which that pivot demonstrably paid off in both top-line growth and cloud profitability.
business_type: Enterprise software and cloud computing (large-cap SaaS/IaaS/PaaS)
macro_context: Accelerating enterprise migration to public cloud; intense hyperscale competition with Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud; broad shift of software economics from perpetual licenses to recurring subscription and consumption revenue.
evidence_summary: Microsoft's deliberate strategic-capex bet on cloud infrastructure converted into durable, profitable growth. In FY2018 total revenue reached $110.4 billion with operating income of $35.1 billion. The Intelligent Cloud segment generated $26.8 billion in revenue, up 21%, with Azure revenue growing 91% year over year. Commercial cloud revenue reached $23.2 billion and, critically, commercial cloud gross margin expanded to 57%, up 7 percentage points year over year, showing the heavy capital investment in datacenters was translating into improving unit economics rather than margin destruction.
owner_decision_context: Leadership chose to commit large, sustained capital expenditure to build out global cloud datacenter capacity and to reorient sales and product strategy around recurring cloud consumption, accepting near-term margin pressure on the bet that scale would drive cloud gross margin expansion over time.
action_taken: Continued heavy investment in Azure datacenter capacity and cloud platform, repositioned Office and Dynamics toward subscription (Office 365 / Dynamics 365), and managed the transition so commercial cloud scaled while improving its gross margin.
outcome_evidence: FY2018 results confirm the strategy worked: Intelligent Cloud up 21% to $26.8B, Azure up 91%, commercial cloud at $23.2B with gross margin expanding 7 points to 57%, alongside company-wide revenue of $110.4B and $35.1B operating income.
source_limitations: WebFetch of sec.gov typically returns HTTP 403 in this environment; all figures were confirmed verbatim in WebSearch snippets attributed to the FY2018 10-K and Microsoft FY2018 investor materials. Segment-internal cost allocations and per-customer unit economics are not separately disclosed and are not asserted here.
directly_stated: FY2018 total revenue was $110.4 billion and operating income was $35.1 billion
Intelligent Cloud revenue was $26.8 billion, up 21% in FY2018
Azure revenue grew 91% year over year in FY2018
Commercial cloud revenue was $23.2 billion with gross margin of 57%, up 7 points year over year
inferred: The simultaneous strong revenue growth and gross-margin expansion in commercial cloud indicates the strategic-capex bet on datacenter scale improved (rather than eroded) cloud unit economics
The packaged-license-to-cloud pivot is best classified as a successful turnaround of the company's strategic and margin trajectory
why_useful_for_opsiq: A clean example of a large incumbent making a high-stakes strategic-capex bet that succeeds: heavy cloud investment produces both growth and improving margins. Tests whether the engine can recognize a deliberate, well-executed strategic pivot as a successful turnaround rather than flagging the capital intensity as risk.
